items.title: Four things to know about Alvin Tedjo, the winner of Mississauga's wild mayoral election
items.summary: He was a first-term councillor and a long-shot candidate. From high school student council to an unlikely win, here’s what to know about Alvin Tedjo. Alvin Tedjo, a first-term councillor, has been elected mayor of Mississauga. He grew up with a view of City Hall outside his house. Now, he will be Mississauga’s mayor. Alvin Tedjo, a first-term councillor and former provincial political staffer, staged an unlikely campaign against two titans of Mississauga politics — former mayor Bonnie Crombie and incumbent Carolyn Parrish — to ride to victory on Monday. Here are four things to know about Tedjo. Tedjo’s Chinese-Indonesian parents settled in Mississauga when he was four and he grew up downtown, where he could see City Hall from outside his house. “I saw a lot of the challenges and hardships that come with that immigrant experience,” he said on a 2025 podcast. “If you see something wrong, do something about it,” he said his parents taught him. He was student council president in high school and served on the mayor’s youth advisory committee. He met then-mayor Hazel McCallion in the mid-1990s, when he won an award for being Young Citizen of the Year. “Get into politics, young man,” she told him, he said.

Alvin Tedjo may have started the Mississauga mayoral election as an underdog, but he has managed to beat out former mayor Bonnie Crombie and incumbent Carolyn Parrish to take over the city’s top job, CityNews projects. He is winning handidly, leading Parrish in second by over 20,000 votes, despite early polls showing a tight race leading up to election. “Our optimism, our hope, our vision for what this city could be, our positivity and our unstoppable effort to reach every single resident in the city of Mississauga, to put forward practical solutions that would make a difference in their lives and to earn their trust, all of that hard work has led us to this moment,” said Tedjo in his victory speech.

items.title: Alvin Tedjo wins Mississauga mayoral race in decisive victory over two political heavyweights
items.summary: Rookie councillor surged from a distant fourth in early polling to beat incumbent Carolyn Parrish and frontrunner Bonnie Crombie. Alvin Tedjo won the Mississauga mayoral race in a decisive win over two local political heavyweights. Rookie councillor Alvin Tedjo has been elected mayor of Mississauga, a stunning against-the-odds victory over a pair of political heavyweights. Tedjo, 43, began his campaign trailing in fourth place, well behind incumbent mayor Carolyn Parrish and former mayor Bonnie Crombie. ” “My friends, Mississauga has voted for change,” Tedjo said to a chorus of cheers at his victory party. “When we started this six months ago, we knew it was going to be tough. People told us we couldn’t win ... ” With 89 per cent of polls reporting, Tedjo led by more than 18,000 votes. Crombie, who held a narrow lead in the polls heading into election day, said she had called Tedjo to congratulate him. The people of Mississauga have “voted for change,” said Crombie, with her three children standing beside her on stage. “Alvin, your energy, your enthusiasm and the joy you bring to politics matter. You’ve inspired people to get involved and to believe that they can help shape the city’s future. That is something to be proud of.

items.title: Brampton Man Surrenders Hours After Police Release His Description in Fatal Mississauga Stabbing
items.summary: Insauga.com reports a Brampton man has been charged with second-degree murder in connection with a deadly stabbing in Mississauga over the weekend. According to Peel Regional Police, the suspect they had been searching for since the stabbing was reported early Sunday morning turned himself in to homicide detectives on Monday afternoon. The outlet reports police had issued a release earlier that day identifying him and urging him to seek legal counsel and surrender. According to the outlet, the stabbing happened in a parking lot in an industrial area near Tomken Road and Kamato Road in Mississauga's east end, where officers found a man with life-threatening injuries who was pronounced dead at the scene despite first responders' efforts. The outlet reports police had earlier described the suspect as a Black man with a large build, long dreadlocked hair and a tattoo of five stars on his left upper cheek. According to insauga.com, Kevin Chippie, 35, of Brampton, turned himself in and was charged with second-degree murder, and the investigation remains ongoing.

items.title: Urban Capital Takes Over Final Three Towers of Mississauga's M City Megaproject
items.summary: Insauga.com reports the remaining development lands at Mississauga's M City condo community have changed hands. According to the outlet, Urban Capital has acquired the land for the project's final three towers, M6, M7 and M8, from Rogers Real Estate Development Limited. The outlet reports M City launched in 2017 at Burnhamthorpe Road West and Confederation Parkway, with five of its eight planned towers, M1 through M5, now completed or under construction, including the 83-storey M3, which Urban Capital says will be the tallest skyscraper in Mississauga. According to insauga.com, the full 15-acre community is planned to eventually include more than 6,000 homes, retail and office space, and over two acres of new public parkland. Mark Reeve, a partner at Urban Capital, told the outlet the company has been involved with M City since the beginning and has a deep connection to the community and its future.

items.title: University of Toronto Professor Calls Mississauga's Mayoral Race Unusually Rare Matchup
items.summary: Insauga.com reports Mississauga's 2026 mayoral race has turned into an unusually tight contest as voters head to the polls. According to the outlet, the campaign began with two clear front-runners, incumbent Mayor Carolyn Parrish and her predecessor Bonnie Crombie, who left the mayor's chair early in 2024 after a decade in office to lead the Ontario Liberal Party. The outlet reports city councillors Alvin Tedjo of Ward 2 and Dipika Damerla of Ward 7 also entered the race with recognizable names, though neither was initially expected to mount a serious challenge. According to insauga.com, recent polling suggests Tedjo has gained enough ground to turn the contest into a genuine three-way race heading into election day. Randy Besco, an associate professor of political science at the University of Toronto Mississauga, told the outlet it is unusual in municipal politics for a sitting mayor to face a serious challenge from her own predecessor, describing it as effectively having two incumbents competing for the same job.
